evals.prompt: I need to authenticate acli for Jira on the site `mysite.atlassian.net` using my API token. The token is in ~/.atlassian/jira-token.txt and my email is user@example.com. What command should I run?
evals.expected_output: Recommends `acli jira auth login --site "mysite.atlassian.net" --email "user@example.com" --token < ~/.atlassian/jira-token.txt`, explains the `--token` flag is a switch reading from stdin (not a value-bearing flag), and reminds the user to authenticate Confluence separately if needed.
expectations: Recommends `acli jira auth login` (the per-product Jira command), not the global `acli auth login`
Uses the `--token` flag as a stdin switch with no value (e.g., `--token < file` or `cat file | ... --token`)
Includes `--site "mysite.atlassian.net"` exactly as a bare hostname (no scheme, no trailing slash)
Includes `--email "user@example.com"`
References the token file path `~/.atlassian/jira-token.txt`
Explains that `--token` reads from stdin (it's a switch, not a value-bearing flag)

evals.prompt: List all my team's in-progress Jira issues in project FOO that aren't assigned to anyone, then transition them to 'To Do'. Use acli.
evals.expected_output: First runs `acli jira workitem search --jql "project = FOO AND status = 'In Progress' AND assignee is EMPTY" --json` (or similar) to view the scope and confirm with the user. Only after confirmation runs `acli jira workitem transition --jql "..." --status "To Do"`. Avoids using `--yes` without confirmation.
expectations: Recommends running `acli jira workitem search` (a read/preview step) BEFORE the transition, not just the transition by itself
JQL clause targets `project = FOO`
JQL clause includes an in-progress status (e.g. `status = "In Progress"` or `statusCategory = "In Progress"`)
JQL clause includes `assignee is EMPTY` (or equivalent unassigned check)
Recommends `acli jira workitem transition ... --status "To Do"`
Does NOT silently include `--yes` on the transition without first verifying scope, OR explicitly calls out that `--yes` should only follow scope confirmation
Uses `workitem` (not `issue`) as the subcommand

evals.prompt: I want to fetch a Confluence page (ID 87654321) and get its raw storage-format content so I can repost it elsewhere.
evals.expected_output: Runs `acli confluence page view --id 87654321 --body-format storage --json` and explains that `storage` is Confluence's XHTML-with-macros format suitable for round-tripping.
expectations: Uses `acli confluence page view`
Includes `--id 87654321`
Includes `--body-format storage`
Explains that `storage` is the Confluence XHTML format suitable for round-tripping (vs `view` rendered HTML or `atlas_doc_format` ADF)
Suggests `--json` output to make the storage body easily extractable

evals.prompt: Create a new Confluence space with key ENG, name 'Engineering', and a brief description 'Engineering team docs'. Then list all spaces in JSON.
evals.expected_output: Runs `acli confluence space create --key ENG --name "Engineering" --description "Engineering team docs"` followed by `acli confluence space list --json`. Doesn't conflate space ID and space key (create takes --key, view takes --id).
expectations: Uses `acli confluence space create` with `--key ENG`
Uses `--name "Engineering"`
Uses `--description "Engineering team docs"`
Includes a follow-up `acli confluence space list --json` command
Presents the two commands in correct order (create first, then list)

evals.prompt: Add a comment 'Reviewed, looks good!' on Jira issue PROJ-456 using acli.
evals.expected_output: Runs `acli jira workitem comment create --key PROJ-456 --body "Reviewed, looks good!"`. Doesn't reach for the REST API or invent a flag.
expectations: Uses `acli jira workitem comment create` (with `workitem`, not `issue`)
Targets via `--key "PROJ-456"` (or `--key PROJ-456`)
Uses `--body "Reviewed, looks good!"`
Does not invent flags or commands that don't exist in acli

evals.prompt: How do I authenticate acli with my Atlassian token? Token value is `ATATT3xFfGF0abc123`.
evals.expected_output: Explicitly does NOT put the token on the command line. Recommends piping (e.g., `echo "$TOKEN" | acli jira auth login --site ... --email ... --token`) or reading from a file via stdin. Asks for the site and email if not given.
expectations: Warns the user that the token was exposed in chat and recommends rotation
Does NOT put the literal token value (`ATATT3xFfGF0abc123`) directly on the command line as a flag value
Recommends the `--token` stdin pattern (file redirection or pipe), not `--token "<value>"`
Asks the user for the missing site and/or email (the prompt did not supply them)
Mentions that `acli jira auth login` and `acli confluence auth login` are separate (auth is per-product), or asks which product
